full_judgment:
2. The facts leading to the issuance of Rule, in short, is that the respondent No. being financial institution filed Artha Rin Suit No.2 of 2007 for recovery of an outstanding dues against the petitioner and ultimately the suit was decreed ex-parte to the tune of Taka 9,22,671. Being failure to pay the decretal dues the decree-holder Bank filed Artha Execution Case No.69 of 2010 for recovery of the decretal dues. Eventually the mortgage property was put into auction on 11-11-2010. Only one bidder namely Md Saleh Zahur participated in the bid offering an amount of Taka 20,40,820. Thereafter, the petitioner judgment- debtor on 10-1-2011 filed an application mentioning section 33(2) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 for setting-aside the auction dated 11-11-2010 alleging, that the auction was held by showing the value of the property in a shocking low price and the petitioner in the meantime deposited outstanding dues of the bank to the tune of Taka 9,23,000. The Adalat after hearing the application filed by the petitioner by observing that the petition was not in form and the judgment-debtor should have been filed an application under Order XXI, rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting-aside the auction and accordingly rejected the application filed by the petitioner by order dated 20-1-2011. 

 4. Mr Lokman Karim, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that misquoting or wrong quoting of provision of law in cause title by itself is no ground for refusal to grant relief if it is otherwise permissible in law but learned Artha Rin Adalat without considering this proposition of law illegally rejected the application filed by the petitioner. The learned Advocate also submits that material irregularities and fraud was committed in the auction process because the decree-holder Bank by mentioning wrong schedule of the property in the execution proceeding as well as in the auction proclamation notice proceeded with the auction and ultimately the property of the judgment-debtor is shown to have been sold in the said auction process. The learned Advocate further submits that though sale has been confirmed in the meantime on the wrong schedule but it will not confer any title upon auction purchaser and the property of the judgment- debtor was not in fact sold in auction. In support of the argument the learned Advocate referred to a decision of Rokeya Begum vs Md Nurul Absar reported in 9 MLR (AD) 285 = 9 BLC (AD) 169. 

 6. Mr Abdul Momen Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the added Respondent No.6, auction purchaser, also opposed the Rule by filing affidavit-in-opposition and submits that under section 65 of the Code of Civil Procedure where an immovable property is sold in execution of decree and such sale has become absolute the property shall be deemed to have vested in the purchaser like i.e. petitioner and, as such, sale cannot be questioned any way without resorting under Order XXI, rule 90 of the code or so like. In support of his submission the learned Advocate relied upon an unreported decision of the case of Mrs Rokeya Afroza vs Judge, Artha Rin Adalat No.4, Dhaka passed in Writ Petition No. 8549 of 2005 where it has been held- 

 "In the light of section 65 of the Code it is crystal clear that where the immovable property is sold in execution of a decree and such sale has become absolute, it shall be deemed to have vested in the purchaser from the time when the property is sold and not from the time when the sale becomes absolute. In other words, it is the confirmation of sale that passes the title and the auction purchaser become the owner of the property from the date of sale unless the sale is set-aside on the ground of fraud and material irregularity" 

 10. From order No.15 dated 13-2-2011 it reveals that after confirmation of sale the decree-holder filed an application for correction of the schedule of the sale certificate by inserting BS plot Nos.1271, 1272 and 1273 in place of BS plot Nos.1171, 1172 and 1172 and accordingly the Adalat directed to correct the plot numbers as prayed by the decree-holder, It is apparent on the face of the record that the decree-holder got the plot numbers of the property correct which was sold in execution of the decree after the confirmation of the sale which is enough to bring the matter within the mischief of Order XXI, rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting-aside auction sale on the ground of material irregularity. It also appears that the judgment-debtor filed an application for setting-aside the auction sale by misquoting section 33(2) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain which should have been filed under Order XXI, rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure as observed by the Adalat. In the decision of Antibiotic Stores vs Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat reported in 55 DLR (AD) 13 = 8 BLD (AD) 8 our apex Court held:- 

 'In the present case the impugned order has been passed in the execution proceeding and the petitioner could avail the provision of Order XXI, rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure in setting-aside the auction sale on ground of material irregularity find fraud alleged by any of the party to the execution proceeding arising out of judgment and decree passed under the Ain as the same could have been adequately dealt with under the said provision, and in the facts and circumstances of the instant case the writ jurisdiction's not maintainable for deciding the question of fraud and material irregularity in publishing and conducting the sale, which are essentially a question of fact to be determined on evidence and could not be conveniently dealt with in wit jurisdiction. Reference in this regard may be made in the case of Sarder Jan-e-Alam vs Arab Bangladesh Bank Ltd. reported in 4 BLC (AD) 178.
